parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and children recognized Node ESM .mjs output, manual argv parsing, zero external modules, ASCII encoding behavior, bencode ordering, Python bytes repr, and no Buffer-like binary APIs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent explored executable behavior, split encoder, decoder, repr, and argparse modules across four subagents, then assigned a fifth child to read those modules, write the entry point, and verify the integrated program.
parallel.implementation: The produced artifact used separate bencode encoder and decoder modules, pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test12.mjs, with strings for byte data, BigInt for integers, arrays, and Map dictionaries.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The entry/verifier child read all four child modules before writing test12.mjs, edited the entry after a Unicode error-format discrepancy, and the status artifact list shows the expected entry and library files were copied.
parallel.verification: Children ran module self-checks, and the entry/verifier compared outputs against the executable across samples and edge cases while noting remaining non-ASCII traceback wrapper differences as exempt.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still marked the parallel solution failed at 142/172; the mounted evidence does not expose individual hidden failed cases beyond the aggregate score.

serial.requirements: The serial main recognized the same ESM, .mjs, argument parsing, output formatting, bencode, ASCII, BigInt, and no typed-array requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent probed the executable, designed a PyBytes-centered value model, wrote every library and the entry point itself, and owned integration and verification end to end.
serial.implementation: The serial artifact used pybytes.mjs, a combined bencode.mjs, pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test12.mjs, with PyBytes objects for byte strings and BigInt for integers.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote all files in one implementation phase and the status artifact list shows the expected test12.mjs entry plus four libraries copied.
serial.verification: The serial run diffed several normal cases, checked equals-form and argument errors, then fixed masked pipeline exit checks and verified missing, bad int, and non-ASCII exit codes.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also marked the serial solution failed at 142/172, so hidden remaining mismatch appears shared rather than parallel-specific from the mounted evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used the same prompt requirements and propagated detailed shared constraints to child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the same prompt and reconstructed reference behavior directly before writing code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-level outcome difference is visible; both recognized the core task and both failed the same official count.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by module into four implementation children and one integration/verifier child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all module, entry, integration, and verification work in one main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit distributed ownership; serial had single-owner execution, but neither ownership model produced a different official outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included a shared value representation, bencode contracts, file ownership, and the no Buffer constraint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial internally chose a PyBytes abstraction and used it consistently across its combined module set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required an explicit cross-agent interface, while serial did not; no concrete incompatible handoff or interface mismatch is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered encoder.mjs, decoder.mjs, pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test12.mjs under a bencode subdirectory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered pybytes.mjs, bencode.mjs, pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test12.mjs as a compact module set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The internal structure differed, but both artifacts covered the same logical functions and reached the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The main parent received the swarm result and then received the entry/verifier child summary before closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to join; the serial main retained all intermediate results locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result lifecycle steps, but completed child results were returned and used in the next delegation or final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote separate module files first, then the entry/verifier child read those modules and wrote the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all generated files from one main actor in one implementation phase.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared workspace coordination but no proven collision, overwrite, or abandoned artifact; serial avoided that class of risk by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children self-checked modules and the verifier child ran an integrated comparison harness before final summary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran executable comparisons and exit-code checks in the main trajectory before declaring completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was delegated and summarized; serial verification was direct. Both claimed local verification but both failed official hidden evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents, more requests and tokens, and 355 agent seconds, but did not time out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests and tokens, and 210 agent seconds, also without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was costlier, but the added cost did not displace required work or cause deadline closure in the evidence.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed cell/status.json evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false with 142 of 172 cases passed. The process difference is that parallel delegated module construction and entry verification across five child agents, while serial implemented and verified directly. The mounted evidence does not reveal a parallel-specific coordination consequence that explains a different official result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposition produced a coherent artifact but incurred extra child-result and integration steps.
The verifier child reported local functional comparisons and a non-ASCII traceback wrapper caveat before final delivery.
serial_contributors: Serial kept implementation and verification in one trajectory with a PyBytes-centered design.
Serial also locally verified sample and edge cases before official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used plain strings plus split encoder and decoder modules; serial used a PyBytes class and a combined bencode module.
Both likely share a hidden behavioral mismatch because the official pass counts are identical, but the mounted summaries do not include per-case failures.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official results are mounted, so individual failing testcase categories cannot be resolved from the allowed inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; no retained parallel coordination pattern
